newsitem.title: USA: Texaco sees $488 mln U.S. tax refund in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Texaco sees $488 mln U.S. tax refund in Q1.

text.p: Texaco Inc expects to book $488 million in its first quarter as a refund from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service after the U.S. Supreme Court refused an application from the IRS to review a lower court decision in Texaco's favor.

Texaco said on Monday that the U.S. court decision in the "Aramco Advantage" case, under which Texaco was limited to the price it could charge for Saudi Arabian crude, meant that the company would receive a total refund of $700 million, mostly this year.
From 1979 through 1981, as a result of a directive from the Saudi government, Texaco was limited in the amount that it could charge for crude oil purchased from Saudi Arabia.
The IRS had claimed that Texaco should pay taxes on the sale of crude oil based on higher prices than Texaco actually received for the oil.
Other companies involved are Chevron Corp and Exxon Corp.
It was not immediately clear where Chevron and Exxon stand on the issue.
